videos.title: Deploy Strapi to production (Heroku)
videos.description:
Deployment: Deploy Strapi to production (Heroku)

In this course, we take a quick look at Strapi v4 and explore it's capabilities, including content type and content management as well as authentication and security.

In the second part of the course, we build a frontend for our data stored in Strapi using Next.js. The application will allow us to register users, create a custom profile with a cool profile image via Cloudinary as well as have certain features enabled only if a user is logged in.

Last but not least, we also take a look at how to deploy a production instance of Strapi to Heroku, plus we also deploy the Next.js app to Vercel.

By completing this course you will become familiar with Strapi and have a thorough understanding of how to integrate your headless CMS data with Next.js.

There are two repositories for this course, one is the Strapi CMS's source and the other is the UI, these can be found here:

videos.description:
Strapi tutorial part 1, we will look at what we will build and set up our initial Strapi project.
👉 Lesson Notes:: https://www.codingafterthirty.com/courses/strapi-5-crash-course-2025/getting-started-with-strapi-5-1
👉 Learn more about Strapi: https://strapi.link/learn-more

This is the only Strapi 5 tutorial you will ever need.  

🚀 Strapi Course Overview – What You’ll Learn

Strapi is a powerful open-source headless CMS that allows you to fully control your content and APIs. This course is designed to help you understand how Strapi works and how to use it effectively in real-world projects.

What We’ll Cover:
- Setting up Strapi from scratch
- Creating and structuring content with collections, single types, and components
- Connecting Strapi to a frontend like Next.js or Astro
- Customizing Strapi to fit specific project needs
- Deploying and maintaining a Strapi project

Why use Strapi

Core Functionality
Strapi 5 is a headless CMS that represents content as API endpoints for front-end access, enabling non-technical users to manage website data through Dynamic Zones and blocks.

The Dynamic Pages feature empowers users to easily add new pages to the frontend by creating blocks with specific data types, facilitating the expansion of an Astro website.

Content Management
Strapi's blocks concept allows developers to create various components with specific data types, enabling flexible content management for non-technical users through the Strapi admin interface.

Dynamic Zones break down each section of a page, allowing for easy management and updates through the Strapi admin, enhancing content flexibility.

API Integration
Strapi exposes API endpoints for seamless front-end access, which is demonstrated by making a GET request to the landing page endpoint for data rendering.

User-Friendly Interface
The content manager facilitates easy website data management by creating collections of different data types, such as Global and Landing Pages, with blocks representing various content elements.

By the end of this course, you'll have a solid grasp of Strapi’s core features and how to integrate them into your workflow. Whether working on a personal project, building for clients, or scaling a larger application, this course will give you the tools you need.p

videos.title: Strapi Authentication Provider - Google
videos.description:
If you enjoyed this video then check out The Complete Strapi Course on Udemy: 
https://www.udemy.com/course/the-complete-strapi-course/?couponCode=STRAPI_JUN_21

In this video, I'll show you how to use Authentication Providers with Strapi.

More specifically, we will set up Google as an OAuth provider.

Since Google requires a live URL, we will be using ngrok to tunnel our localhost to a live website.

You could also deploy your app to Heroku to get a similar result.

SET UP STRAPI
For this project, I'm installing a fresh new Strapi with
npx create-strapi-app strapi-auth-demo --quickstart.

However, there is no need for any particular installation. 
As long as you are using Strapi 3.0.0 or higher, you should be good to go.

Once Strapi is ready, we can tunnel it with ngrok.

DOWNLOAD NGROK
Google requires using a real domain when setting up OAuth.
The simplest solution is to tunnel our Strapi Install throuhg ngrok

ngrok makes your localhost publicly accessible to the internet

Navigate to ngrok.com
Click on Get Started For Free
Register or Login
Download ngrok

UNZIP NGROK
To use Ngrok, open a terminal window
Navigate to the Downloads folder
Copy and paste the command that you see on step 2 of the installation process

Then run ngrok while listening to port 1337

You will see two URLs, an HTTP and an HTTPS URL.
Pick whichever you prefer (I'd recommend the HTTPS version).

Now it's time to Set up the Google API Project.

SET UP 
Navigate to console.developers.google.com
If you don't have an account, follow the on-screen instructions to create one. You may have to set up billing to validate your account. 
However, Google offers a free tier.

Then click on the top left to open up your list of projects.
Then click on "New Project" on the right.

Give your project a name, in my case Strapi Auth Demo.
Then click on the OAuth consent screen on the left.
Set it to  external and create it

Set the name of the application
in my case Star auth demo
Do not put a logo to avoid having it validate your OAuth Screen manually which will lose time

Add homepage, privacy policy, and terms of service.
You could use the public folder for these.
I'll set them to the Strapi Base Url since this is a toy project.

Then save.

Now click on credentials.
Click on create credentials in the top select OAuth client id

Set application type to "Web Application". 
Give your application a name; I'll call mine Strapi.

Set the authorized origins to be the ngrok URL.

Copy the domain from ngrok and paste it the Authorized JavaScript origins

For Authorized redirect URIs paste the ngrok domain followed up by
/connect/google/callback,
This is the URL that strapi will forward us to along with the User Credentials.

Click on Save.

Now it's time to try this out.

TRY IT OUT WITH BUG
Navigate to your ngrok URL
Then add /connect/google.

You should see an error message 400: invalid request.
That will read:
Invalid parameter value for redirect_uri: Missing scheme: /connect/google/callback

This is because Strapi doesn't know which URL to use when setting up the redirect_url.
This parameter is set as config.server.url, which at this time is empty.

TRY IT OUT FIXED
In order to set it up properly, open up the Strapi code with your IDE.
Open /config/server.js

Add a new line:
URL: 
And set it to be the ngrok URL without a trailing slash.

Let the server restart and try again.

You should now be able to connect with your Google Provider and will receive back a Strapi User Object.

Note that you can still use Strapi Locally even if you set the URL.

The only annoyance will be that you have to set a different URL for Production and for Development.

MAKING THIS WORK WITH SPA
You have successfully retrieved the user object, but you're stuck in the Strapi application. 
What if you wanted to use this for your Single Page Application?

You can start by chaning the Setting in the Strapi Google Provider, under
The redirect URL to your front-end app
Set that to the URL of your app.

On Successful login, you'll be forwarded to your application with a query string containing a bearer token.

Use the bearer token in the query String to make a get request to:
Your ngrok URL /auth/google/callback

As a demo I'm just going to copy and paste the entire set of query parameters.

Your get request will then return you the Strapi user object, along with a JWT token you can use to make authenticated Requests

CONCLUSION
So there you have it using Google as an Authentication Provider.
 
Please like the video if you've enjoyed it, make sure to subscribe for more and leave a comment telling me which topics to cover next.

If you want to take your Strapi learning even further, make sure to check out the Complete Strapi Course, available on Udemy, link in the description.

Thank you for watching, and have an awesome day!

https://www.udemy.com/course/the-complete-strapi-course/?couponCode=STRAPI_JUN_21

Note this course uses Next version 12 you can find an updated Next.js 14 tutorial here https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PL7Q0DQYATmvgONvIWsy34aDkAtcdjsQLE&feature=shared

Creating the UI using Next.js: Authentication with Next.js and Strapi (part 1)

In this course, we take a quick look at Strapi v4 and explore it's capabilities, including content type and content management as well as authentication and security.

In the second part of the course, we build a frontend for our data stored in Strapi using Next.js. The application will allow us to register users, create a custom profile with a cool profile image via Cloudinary as well as have certain features enabled only if a user is logged in.

Last but not least, we also take a look at how to deploy a production instance of Strapi to Heroku, plus we also deploy the Next.js app to Vercel.

By completing this course you will become familiar with Strapi and have a thorough understanding of how to integrate your headless CMS data with Next.js.

There are two repositories for this course, one is the Strapi CMS's source and the other is the UI, these can be found here:
-Strapi Headless CMS: https://github.com/tpiros/jamstack-training-films-cms
-UI: https://github.com/tpiros/jamstack-training-films-ui
